small_guidance:
- Add larger autotune configs targeting M=1024, N=8192, K=8192: try BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 and BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4 to better overlap the large-K loop.
- Introduce a GROUP_M block-swizzle (group size 8) so program scheduling reuses L2 across N tiles within an M-row group — this is a known win for big GEMMs on Ada.
- Drop the per-iteration K mask since K=8192 is divisible by BLOCK_K candidates (32/64); use unmasked loads inside the loop and only mask on the M/N edges to cut predicate overhead.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a persistent/split-K GEMM epilogue-fused kernel: with M=1024, N=8192, K=8192 and only 8x64=512 M/N tiles for 128x128, the SM occupancy on a 4090 (128 SMs) is fine, but a persistent kernel with a swizzled tile iterator avoids launcher overhead and improves L2 reuse across waves.
- Pre-transpose the weight to (K, N) layout once in __init__ so the inner loop loads B contiguously along N (the dot's inner axis) — current layout has W as (N, K) with stride_wk on the K axis, forcing strided B loads.
- Consider TF32 `tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` (the activations are bounded post-clamp/tanh so the 5e-2 tolerance is comfortable) — this can roughly double Tensor Core throughput on the K=8192 reduction.
